title: Aboriginal kids have a built-in compass — they can't get lost
voiceover: There's an aboriginal community in Australia where children, by age five, can tell you which way is north. Always. Even with their eyes closed. Even underground. Even in a completely unfamiliar room. They don't think in terms of left and right. They think in terms of cardinal directions. Their language doesn't even have a word for left. Brain scans show their hippocampus develops differently. They built an internal compass. The wild thing — every human is capable of this. We just stopped using it. Our phones killed something we used to have for free. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
